clarifyingQuestions: Should scan return keys, values, or key/value pairs?
Should expired keys be eagerly deleted or lazily cleaned on access?
followUps: Add compare-and-set where expired keys behave as missing.
Add a snapshot method with deterministic ordering.
Add thread safety with one lock around the item map and expiry checks.
followUpGuide: For compare-and-set, sample time once and call the same live-read helper with that sample. Expired keys count as missing; compare and replacement must be one atomic operation under concurrency.

For a snapshot, scan("") already returns a new sorted list of pairs. Since this exercise stores strings, later overwrites cannot mutate earlier returned values. Arbitrary mutable values would require a separate copying or immutability contract.
For thread safety, wrap every method with one `threading.RLock`. Keep expiry cleanup and mutation inside the same critical section.
complexityAnalysis: - Supplied lazy expiry: Time: O(1) average for set/get/delete and O(N + K log K) for scan, with N retained keys and K matching live keys, treating string operations as bounded-cost. Space: O(N) retained state and O(N + K) temporary scan/output space. Expired entries can remain until accessed or scanned.

- Heap expiry follow-up: processing E expired or stale heap records costs O(E log H), with H heap entries; inserting a deadline costs O(log H). Overwrites need version checks so stale deadlines cannot delete replacements. H can exceed live key count unless stale entries are compacted. Sorted scan results still cost O(N + K log K) plus cleanup.

- Ordered-key index follow-up: a balanced tree locates the prefix range in O(log N), then visits M matching candidates to test expiry, costing O(log N + M) plus output. M includes expired candidates. Python bisect searches a sorted list in O(log N), but inserting into that list is O(N).
solutionGuide: Store each value with an optional `expires_at`. Injecting `now` gives deterministic tests and avoids sleeps.
Every operation samples now once and passes that sample into its live-read helper. This keeps one scan consistent even if the injected clock advances while checking keys.
